etymology: Simplified from 醫: an arrow (矢) in a surgeon's box (匚) — the healer who pulls arrowheads from wounds: doctor.
mnemonic: Open the doctor's case: inside, the arrow he just removed — イ. The 医者 keeps every arrow life fires at you.

etymology: Originally the round mouth (口) of a bronze tripod vessel (貝-shaped below) — 'round' was borrowed long ago for counting people: member, personnel.
mnemonic: A mouth to feed sitting on the payroll money (貝): one head counted — イン. 店員, 会社員, 駅員: wherever there's a counter, there's an 員 behind it.

etymology: Phono-semantic: wall/mound (阝) + 完 'complete' (phonetic イン) — a compound completely enclosed by walls: an institution.
mnemonic: Walls (阝) all the way around until the enclosure is complete (完): hospital, temple, academy — イン. 病院: the walled place you'd rather visit than inhabit.

etymology: Phono-semantic: movement (辶) + 軍 'army' (phonetic ウン) — army wagons rolling supplies down the road: to transport; and the fortune that rolls with the convoy.
mnemonic: The supply wagons roll: whatever they bring you is your luck — はこぶ, ウン. 運転 is keeping your own wagon on the road; 運がいい is when the road is kind.

etymology: Compound: a low covering (尸) over 至 'arrive' — the shelter you arrive under: roof, house; in Japanese, the shop and its keeper (〜屋).
mnemonic: Duck under the low roof: you've arrived at the shop — や. 本屋, パン屋, 花屋 — every trade gets its own little roof.

etymology: Phono-semantic: field (田) + 介 'between' (phonetic カイ) — the dividing ridges between fields: boundaries, and the bounded whole they define — the world.
mnemonic: Stand on the ridge between two paddies: every world is fields plus fences — カイ. 世界: all the fields, all the fences, seen at once.

etymology: Compound ideograph: two hands (开) lifting the bar from inside the gate (門) — to open.
mnemonic: Both hands on the crossbar, lift, and the gate swings — あける, ひらく. The elevator button says 開: hands off the bar, doors open.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a person packed in straw under a roof, ice (冫) at the bottom — winter insulation, ancient style: cold.
mnemonic: Stuffed under the blankets, hay in the walls, and still two icicles at your feet — さむい. Cold enough that even the kanji is bundled up.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + a phonetic — the Han River, which named the Han dynasty, which named the Chinese script itself: 漢字.
mnemonic: A river (氵) so important a dynasty took its name, and the dynasty named the characters — カン. Every 漢字 you learn flows out of that one river.

etymology: Phono-semantic: food (飠) + 官 'official' (phonetic カン) — the official guesthouse where envoys were fed: a grand building, a hall.
mnemonic: The building big enough to feed officials — カン. Libraries (図書館), cinemas (映画館), embassies (大使館): if it has marble floors, it ends in 館.

etymology: Phono-semantic: run (走) + 己 'self' (phonetic キ) — the self getting up and breaking into a run: to rise, to wake, to start.
mnemonic: The alarm rings and your self (己) launches into a sprint (走) — おきる. Every day 起きる is the first race you win or lose.

etymology: Compound: a hand reaching to catch someone ahead (an old form of 及) over a heart (心) — the heart straining to catch up: hurry, urgent.
mnemonic: Your hand grabs for the closing train door and your heart slams — いそぐ. 急行: the train for hearts in exactly that state.

etymology: Phono-semantic: hole (穴) + 九 (phonetic キュウ) — probing a cave to its very last turn: to investigate exhaustively.
mnemonic: Crawl into the cave (穴) nine (九) turns deep, to the very end — キュウ. 研究 is refusing to stop at turn eight.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a figure striding away from a hollow or dwelling (厶) — departed: gone; of time, the past.
mnemonic: Footsteps walking away from the empty nest — さる. 去年 is the year that walked off and isn't coming back.

etymology: Pictograph: a notched wooden rack for hanging bells and drums — the equipment of one's craft: work, trade, vocation (and karma, in the temples).
mnemonic: Your tools hung on the rack in their notches: that rack is your trade — ギョウ. 卒業 is the day you hang them up at school for the last time.

etymology: Phono-semantic: metal (金) + 艮 (phonetic ギン) — the metal that stands second to gold: silver.
mnemonic: Gold's quieter sibling, same mine, one shade paler — ギン. Banks (銀行) are where silver goes to work; the Ginza is where it goes to shop.

etymology: Simplified from 區: a box (匚) crowded with mouths/households (品, reduced to メ) — a district full of homes: a ward.
mnemonic: One drawer of the city's filing cabinet, an X marking your neighborhood — ク. 渋谷区, 新宿区: Tokyo is a cabinet of 23 drawers.

etymology: Phono-semantic: cart (車) + 圣 (simplified 巠, phonetic ケイ) — a cart light enough to fly down the road: lightweight.
mnemonic: A cart loaded with nothing but thread: the horse barely notices — かるい. 軽自動車: the modern featherweight cart.

etymology: Compound: stone (石) + 开 'made level/even' — grinding on a stone until flat and sharp: to polish; figuratively, to grind at a subject.
mnemonic: Blade on the whetstone, back and forth until it gleams level — と(ぐ). 研究: polishing a question until it cuts.

etymology: Simplified from 縣, which grimly showed a head hung upside-down by a cord — the original sense was 'to suspend' (ancestor of 懸); borrowed for the administrative district 'suspended' from the capital.
mnemonic: A watchful eye (目) hanging from the capital by a thread: local government — ケン. All 43 県 dangle from Tokyo on the same string.

etymology: Phono-semantic: person (亻) + 士 'gentleman-retainer' (phonetic シ) — a person in service to a lord: to serve, to work.
mnemonic: A person standing at the gentleman's side, ready — つかえる. 仕事 is the modern lord: service, five days a week.

etymology: Compound: person (亻) + 吏 'official' — a person dispatched on official business: an envoy; to employ, to use.
mnemonic: The boss points: you, go — you've been used, err, dispatched — つかう. The 大使 is the grandest errand-runner of all: the ambassador.

etymology: Phono-semantic: woman (女) + 台 (phonetic シ) — the ancients located every beginning in the mother: to begin.
mnemonic: Every story starts the same way: a woman (女) on the stage (台) — はじめる. 始めまして: 'we are at the beginning', the first greeting.

etymology: Compound ideograph: bare bones (歹) with a person kneeling beside them (匕) — the mourner at the remains: death.
mnemonic: Someone kneels by what is left — しぬ. The number four (シ) shares its sound, which is why hospitals skip the 4th floor.

etymology: Pictograph: a hand gripping a writing tablet or flagged pole — official business being recorded: an affair, a matter, the abstract 'thing'.
mnemonic: A clerk's hand skewering paperwork on a spike — こと. Intangible things only: 仕事 the work-thing, 食事 the meal-thing, 大事 the thing that matters.

etymology: Phono-semantic: hand (扌) + 寺 'temple' (phonetic ジ) — the hand that grips and keeps: to hold, to possess.
mnemonic: Hold it the way a temple holds its relics: firmly, forever — もつ. 気持ち is what your heart is currently holding.

etymology: Simplified from 寫, originally 'to transfer things into a house' — transferring an image onto paper: to copy, to photograph.
mnemonic: Slip the sheet under the cover (冖) and trace what shows through (与) — うつす. 写真: reality, transferred and 'true'.

etymology: Originally a picture of firewood boiling something (the root of 煮), borrowed since antiquity for 'the one who…' — the all-purpose person suffix.
mnemonic: An old-timer (耂) telling stories in the sun (日): 'the one who…' — もの, シャ. 医者, 学者, 記者 — name the deed and 者 names the doer.

etymology: Pictograph: an oil lamp with its flame (the dot) — the master of the house keeps the lamp burning: lord, chief, main.
mnemonic: One flame on the lampstand and the whole household orbits it — ぬし, シュ. The 主人 is whoever tends the flame; the 主 idea is the one lit brightest.

etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + 冬 'winter' (phonetic シュウ) — the year's thread wound up at winter: to end.
mnemonic: Wind the last of the thread as the first ice forms: done — おわる. 終電: the day's thread runs out at the station.

etymology: Compound ideograph: young wings (羽) over 白 (originally the sun/self) — a fledgling flapping day after day until flight comes: to learn by repetition.
mnemonic: Little wings beating over the nest every single morning — ならう. 練習, 復習: learning is just flapping, counted in days.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a bird (隹) on a tree (木) — the old form had three birds: a flock settling at dusk: to gather.
mnemonic: One tree, and every bird in the valley lands on it at sunset — あつまる. 集合! and the flock assembles.

etymology: Phono-semantic: person (亻) + 主 'the lamp of the master' (phonetic ジュウ) — the person beside the burning lamp: to dwell.
mnemonic: Where your lamp (主) burns, that's where you live — すむ. 住所 is the map coordinate of your flame.

etymology: Pictograph: a person bent under a heavy sack pressing toward the ground — heavy; and layers stacked one on another (かさねる).
mnemonic: The porter's silhouette compressed by the load, stroke stacked on stroke — おもい. Heavy things pile: 重ねる; important things weigh: 大事×重 = 重要.

etymology: Phono-semantic: door (戸) + axe (斤, phonetic ショ) — where the axe rings by the doorway: the spot, the place.
mnemonic: You can find the woodcutter's house with your eyes closed: follow the axe sound to the door — ところ. 台所, 住所, 場所 — every 'where' ends here.

etymology: Phono-semantic: sun (日) + 者 (phonetic ショ — whose own origin is 'boiling') — the sun boiling the air: sultry heat.
mnemonic: The sun sets the kettle of the sky to boil — あつい. August in Japan: the 者 under the 日 is you, simmering.

etymology: Simplified from 乘: a person standing high in a tree, feet on the branches — climbing aboard: to ride, to mount.
mnemonic: Climb the trunk, settle on the highest branch: all aboard — のる. Same move at the station every morning: 電車に乗る.

etymology: Simplified from 眞: a filled vessel set perfectly upright — full to the brim, not a drop false: genuine, true.
mnemonic: Ten (十) eyes (目) inspected it on one (一) bench: certified true — まこと, シン. 写真 is 'the true copy'; 真ん中 the true middle.

etymology: Compound ideograph: movement (辶) + bird (隹) — birds cannot fly backward: to advance, only forward.
mnemonic: A bird on the road has one gear: forward — すすむ. When you can't reverse, every step is 前進.

etymology: Ideograph: three tens (十) joined at the base — thirty years: the span of one generation; then the world that generation inhabits.
mnemonic: Thirty years welded into one bracket: your allotted lap — よ, セ. 世界 is all the laps being run at once; お世話 is helping someone through theirs.

etymology: Phono-semantic: movement (辶) + a phonetic showing hands lifting an offering — walking a gift or a guest on their way: to send, to see off.
mnemonic: Carry the parcel down the road with both hands until the road takes over — おくる. 見送り is when it's a person, and you wave until the train is gone.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a banner with an arrow beneath it — the clan mustered under its standard, arrows ready: tribe, family line.
mnemonic: One flag, everyone's arrows stacked beneath it: that's a family — ゾク. 家族: the tribe whose banner hangs at your door.

etymology: Phono-semantic: step (彳) + 寺 'temple' (phonetic タイ) — pacing back and forth before the temple where you were told to be: to wait.
mnemonic: Little steps in front of the temple gate, checking the road again — まつ. ちょっと待って: two more paces, they'll come.

etymology: Phono-semantic: person (亻) + 弋 'stake, tally' (phonetic ダイ) — one person staked in for another: substitute; the tally of reigns: era; the tally of payment: fee.
mnemonic: Plant a stake where you stood and someone takes your shift — かわる. Eras substitute for eras (時代), coins for goods (電気代): the same swap, three sizes.
